negative_findings.description: Across NLB, OTP banka, Gorenjska banka and Delavska hranilnica announcements surfaced in this run, the technology partner is usually NOT named. Banks describe the customer benefit ('prenovljena mobilna banka', 'nova izkušnja digitalnega bančništva') and omit the supplier.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches combining bank names with 'v sodelovanju z' / 'in partnership with' returned launch stories but almost no explicit vendor attribution; the clearest exception was Addiko naming the state SI-PASS eID service.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The buyer-side cell cannot be relied on alone for vendor attribution. It must be joined to vendor case studies (A6 vendor cell) and to procurement records, with the bank release supplying date and scope rather than the partner name.

negative_findings.description: Several smaller institutions (Primorska hranilnica Vipava, Deželna banka Slovenije, BKS Bank Slovenia branch, Hranilnica LON) surfaced with product and location pages but no discoverable press-release section in these searches.
negative_findings.result_summary: sl-language queries returned homepages, product pages and third-party aggregator profiles rather than any 'sporočila za javnost' or 'novice' index for these institutions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For the tail of the market, technology change must be inferred from product-page and T&C diffs rather than announcements — a different, slower collection method that must be planned for explicitly.

negative_findings.description: Nova KBM and SKB banka ceased to exist as brands and merged into OTP banka; Abanka, Sberbank/N Banka and Summit Leasing have likewise been absorbed. Their historical newsrooms are at risk of disappearing.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search results confirm the NKBM+SKB to OTP merger completion and the migration of customers to unified digital channels; legacy domains were not confirmed live in this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Pre-merger go-live announcements are the record of which vendors those banks bought. If nkbm.si and skb.si are retired without archival, that history is lost — archive.org captures should be secured now.

negative_findings.description: Newsroom URLs for Banka Sparkasse (sparkasse.si), Hranilnica LON (lon.si), UniCredit Banka Slovenija and BKS Bank Slovenia were inferred from brand names and regulator register entries, not observed in search results.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Banka Slovenije supervised-entity register confirmed the legal entities exist; the corporate domains and their news paths were not directly observed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These must be resolved by the deterministic liveness pass before being treated as sources; recording them as confirmed would violate the no-fabrication rule.

negative_findings.description: No Slovenian bank technology/engineering blog (the kind that describes architecture and named platforms) was found in this run — neither in Slovenian nor English.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries for bank digital-transformation pages returned marketing and strategy pages only; the nearest equivalent is the ZBS 'posvet informatikov' conference release and the SRC integrator magazine.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Removes the richest potential buyer-side technical source category for this market. Conference proceedings and integrator publications must substitute.

brief: Slovenia's buyer side is a small, highly consolidated field — roughly a dozen banks and savings banks, best enumerated from the Banka Slovenije supervised-entity register and the ZBS membership rather than from search. Every significant institution publishes go-lives in Slovenian on its own site, but in three different shapes: NLB runs a proper dated press-release archive, OTP banka and Gorenjska banka use flat news/article slugs, and Addiko, Delavska hranilnica and the smaller hranilnice bury the same information in 'obvestila za stranke' and dated terms-and-conditions PDFs. The dominant limitation is that these announcements describe the customer benefit and almost never name the technology partner, so this cell should be treated as the authoritative source of date, scope and institution, to be joined against vendor case studies, annual-report outsourcing disclosures and public procurement for attribution. Highest-value additions next are the shared national rails (Bankart, Flik, SI-PASS/Rekono), annual-report IT sections, and Wayback captures of the retired Nova KBM, SKB, Abanka and Sberbank newsrooms before that history disappears.
